intent: Show that the average highest mathematics course completed by high school graduates was higher in 2004 than in 1982.

requirements.question: How did the average highest mathematics course change between 1982 and 2004?
Are all data marks declared by G0 present in the required state or states?

scope.selection: all data rows (table has no role column)

units.claim: The average highest mathematics level rises from about 2.7 in 1982, between Algebra I and Algebra II and nearer Algebra II, to about 3.65 in 2004, close to Trigonometry/Algebra III.
accept: the 2004 bar is higher than the 1982 bar
1982 is between Algebra I and Algebra II while 2004 is close to Trigonometry/Algebra III
2.7 in 1982 versus 3.65 in 2004 on the displayed ordinal scale
an increase of about 0.95 ordinal levels
reject: saying the level fell from 1982 to 2004
placing 2004 nearer Algebra I than Trigonometry/Algebra III
omitting the 2004 bar or misplacing it below the Algebra II level
units.evidence: Both bars are present on the same ordinal y-axis: the 1982 bar sits between Algebra I and Algebra II, while the taller 2004 bar reaches near Trigonometry/Algebra III.

units.claim: All 2 required bar marks or stacked segments appear in the final chart.
accept: all 2 required data marks are visible
the complete required mark set is present in the final chart
reject: omitting any required bar or stacked segment
replacing missing marks with a summary total or subtitle
units.evidence: G0 data-row coverage is rendered as a complete set of identifiable bar marks.

optional_valid: The 1982 and 2004 values are estimated positions on the displayed ordinal scale; their exact numeric labels are not printed.
